questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code encrypts telemetry at rest? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
An attacker with database write access copies a sealed blob from device A's row into a row belonging to device B. What happens when recent() is called for device B?
choices: The reading is returned as if device B had sent it
openReading() throws because the deviceId is bound as additional authenticated data
The row is skipped silently and the remaining readings are returned
The reading is decrypted but its gps field is dropped

questions.prompt: After activeKeyId is rotated to a new key, what is required for old rows to remain readable through recent()?
choices: Nothing; recent() only works on rows already rewrapped
Only the new key, because GCM can decrypt with any key from the same ring
The old IVs must be regenerated with the new key id
The old key must stay in ring.keys until rewrapOlderThan() has migrated those rows

questions.prompt: Which reading fields are protected by encryption at rest in the telemetry table?
choices: All fields including device_id and recorded_at
Only gps, because the other fields are numeric
gps, batteryPct and sensors; device_id and recorded_at stay in plaintext columns
None; the sealed column stores base64 that anyone can decode
